related.name: Free-Space Path Loss & Link Budget Calculator

method: Computes a theoretical Ethernet frame rate from a MAC line rate and a layer-2 payload size. Wire accounting per frame: 8 bytes of preamble and start-frame delimiter, the 14-byte destination/source/length header, 4 bytes for each selected 802.1Q tag (0, 1 or 2 tags), the entered payload, a 4-byte frame check sequence and a 12-byte inter-frame gap. When header, payload and FCS total fewer than 64 bytes the frame is padded to that IEEE 802.3 minimum; padding is counted on the wire and in overhead but never as payload. Frames per second are line bits per second divided by the 8-bit wire size, the whole-frame figure is the floor of that rate, payload throughput is frames per second multiplied by payload bytes and 8 bits, and efficiency is payload bytes divided by wire bytes. The rate must be a whole number of kb/s between 1 kb/s and 1,600 Gb/s, so decimal input is converted exactly rather than through binary floating point. Payloads run from 1 to 65,535 bytes; anything above 1,500 bytes is flagged as a jumbo frame, which IEEE 802.3 does not define. The model assumes a saturated link and excludes collisions, pause frames, frame preemption, forward error correction, 64b/66b or 8b/10b line coding (10GBASE-R runs at 10.3125 Gbaud), protocol or transport behaviour, address learning, buffering, latency and congestion, so results are maxima rather than measured throughput. It models one frame size at a time, not a traffic mix, and computes no packet capture or network access.
